text: Six lessons, six pieces. This one puts them together into a checklist you can run on any set of tables.

Sort tables into fact and dimension. Arrange them as a star. Create every relationship you need. Check cardinality — many-to-one, fact pointing at dimension, is what you'll see most. Set cross filter direction on purpose. And resolve any table connected more than one way. Here's a real model built that way: Sales at the center, everything else connected directly around it.

Not every real model stays this simple. Here, Sales and Purchases are both fact-like tables, sharing dimensions between them. Read it the same way: trace each line, confirm the cardinality, and watch for loops.
Whatever else grows more complex, the goal never changes: one fact table doing the summarizing, dimension tables doing the filtering.

A correct model is what makes the next chapter possible. DAX depends entirely on your relationships to know which rows to sum, count, or average — get the model right, and DAX becomes trustworthy. Next up: Chapter Five, DAX Fundamentals.
